title: Chicken Tikka Masala
subtitle: Charred chicken in buttery tomato-cream sauce
excerpt: Grilled chicken tikka pieces finished in a rich, spiced tomato and cream sauce. Possibly Britain's most popular dish, and much better made at home than bought.

recipe.sourceNotes: Chicken tikka masala is thought to have been created in Britain, though its origins are debated, attributed variously to Glaswegian or London restaurants in the 1970s. It was named Britain's national dish by Foreign Secretary Robin Cook in 2001. The sauce is a British-Indian invention with no direct equivalent in Indian regional cooking.

content.text: Chicken tikka masala is two recipes in one: the tikka (spiced, grilled chicken) and the masala (the buttery tomato-cream sauce). The tikka is done first, then added to the sauce to finish. The charred edges of the grilled chicken are what make this different from a chicken in sauce, that slight smokiness against the sweet tomato base is the point.

items.preparation: boneless, skinless, cut into 4 cm cubes

content.text: Mix the yoghurt with 1 teaspoon of garam masala, the chilli powder, turmeric, lemon juice, and half the salt. Add the chicken, coat thoroughly, and marinate for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Thread the chicken onto metal skewers and grill under the highest possible heat for 8 to 10 minutes per side until charred at the edges and cooked through. Set aside.
Heat the butter and oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onions for 15 minutes until golden and very soft. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the ground coriander, cumin, and remaining garam masala. Stir for 1 minute. Add the tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes. Add the tinned tomatoes and remaining salt. Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens and the oil separates at the edges.

Add the grilled chicken pieces to the sauce. Pour in the cream and stir. Simmer for 5 minutes to let the chicken absorb the sauce. Taste for salt. Scatter over the coriander and serve with pilau rice or naan.
